{"skill_name": "code-map", "instructions": "# code-map

Run with `run_skill_script(skill_name="code-map", file_path="scripts/code_map.py", args=[COMMAND, NAME])`.
`args` is a list of strings.

| Command | args example | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| find | `["find", "solve_dependencies"]` | qualified node name, `file:start-end`, signature |
| callers | `["callers", "solve_dependencies"]` | every call site: `file:line`, enclosing function, source line |
| callees | `["callees", "solve_dependencies"]` | names called inside that function |
| outline | `["outline", "fastapi/routing.py"]` | classes/functions of one file with line ranges |

- Add `"--tests"` to include test files; add `"--limit", "50"` for more rows.
- NAME can be bare (`get_dependant`), `Class.method`, or a dotted path.
- The qualified name printed by `find` (e.g. `fastapi.dependencies.utils.solve_dependencies`) is the exact `node` to pass to `get_code_neighbors` and `search_similar_code`.", "frontmatter": {"name": "code-map", "description": "Structural code lookup with Python ast. steps.message:
The issue description provided is very generic ("updating the markdown styling within the library"), but based on the codebase analysis of `rich/markdown.py`, the markdown styling is implemented using a set of style names (e.g., `markdown.paragraph`, `markdown.h1`, `markdown.code_block`, `markdown.link`, `markdown.link_url`, `markdown.item.bullet`, `markdown.item.number`, `markdown.hr`).

The current implementation uses `console.get_style("markdown.xxx", default="none")` for several elements, which means if the user hasn't defined a custom style for these, they will be rendered with no special styling (default text).

Without a specific bug report or a set of required style changes, I have identified the locations where markdown styling is applied. If the goal is to provide default styles or change how styles are looked up, these are the key areas.

FILE: rich/markdown.py
LINES: 110, 140, 153, 165, 190, 221, 360, 372, 388, 599, 610, 616
FUNCTION: Various (Paragraph, Heading, CodeBlock, BlockQuote, HorizontalRule, ListItem, Markdown.__rich_console__)
ROOT_CAUSE: The markdown styling currently relies on `console.get_style` with a default of `"none"`, meaning no default visual styling is applied unless the user provides a theme.
PROPOSED_CHANGE: Update the `default="none"` arguments to more appropriate default styles (e.g., `default="cyan"` for links) or introduce a default theme for markdown elements.
OTHER_LOCATIONS: none
TEST_FILE: tests/test_markdown.py
CONFIDENCE: medium
